name: Chipotle Fajita Quesadilla
desc: Steak and fajita peppers folded into a cheesy tortilla, oven-crisped, with a chipotle sour cream dip.

source.title: Copycat Chipotle Steak Quesadillas
source.evidence: Same copycat of Chipotle's fajita quesadilla: steak with cumin and smoked paprika, sliced onion and bell pepper, Monterey Jack, and a dip of sour cream stirred into chipotle honey vinaigrette.

ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for brushing
1 pinch kosher salt, for the vegetables
1/2 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 tsp kosher salt, for the steak
1/2 tsp chili powder or chipotle powder
1/4 cup chipotle honey vinaigrette (store-bought or homemade)

steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and peppers with the pinch of salt, stirring occasionally, until soft and browned in spots, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Preheat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the steak, salt, cumin, paprika, and chili powder and cook, stirring, until browned outside, 3 to 4 minutes.

Brush one side of each tortilla with oil and lay them oiled side down on the baking sheet. Over one half of each, layer 1/2 cup cheese, half the vegetables, half the steak, and another 1/2 cup cheese, then fold in half.
Bake until golden and the cheese is melted, about 8 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Stir the sour cream and chipotle vinaigrette together. Cut the quesadillas into wedges and serve with the dip.
tips: Yellow Bliss Road marinates the steak in adobo and crisps the quesadillas in a skillet over medium-low heat, 2 to 4 minutes per side, if you would rather skip the oven.
